opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Maximum allowed is write; recommend granting write (requested admin exceeds max).
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB for E008 (Karen Black) shows contractor with basic security training, contradicting the earlier note's full-time status. As a contractor, admin is never permitted; write requires advanced training (she has basic). Maximum allowed is read, and requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requests admin to Source Code, but admin is not permitted under any reading of the notes: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Payroll Specialist does not own it. The Security note (which explicitly reviewed its own database) identifies her as a contractor with basic security training, contradicting the HR note's full-time status. As a contractor, write requires advanced training (she has basic), so the maximum permitted level is read. Requested admin exceeds the max, so grant read.
